name: Sree Padmanabhaswamy Temple
tagline: The reclining Vishnu at the heart of the Travancore capital
summary: Sree Padmanabhaswamy Temple in Thiruvananthapuram: Dravidian-Kerala architecture, a reclining Vishnu, strict dress code and the legend of its founding.
description: Sree Padmanabhaswamy Temple stands inside the old fort of Thiruvananthapuram and is dedicated to Vishnu in his reclining form, Anantha Padmanabha, resting on the serpent Ananta. The temple is closely tied to the identity of the former Travancore kingdom, whose rulers dedicated the realm to the deity.

The sanctum is entered through three doors, through which the deity is seen in parts: the face and chest, the navel and Brahma, and the feet. The gopuram, corridors and carved pillars combine Dravidian and Kerala temple styles.

folklore.title: The Child, the Tree and the Sage
story: Local tradition tells of a devout sage, Divakara Muni (also remembered as Vilwamangalath Swamiyar), who prayed to see Vishnu. The god appeared to him as a mischievous child. When the sage tried to hold the child, the boy slipped away and disappeared into a tree.

The tree is said to have fallen and taken the form of Vishnu reclining on Ananta, stretching across a vast distance. The sage asked the deity to become smaller so that he could be worshipped, and the form was reduced until it could be seen through the three doors that devotees use today.
folklore.note: Retold from local tradition; versions differ between sources.

highlights: Reclining Vishnu seen through three doors
Part of the Travancore royal heritage

visitorInfo.bestTime: October to March for cooler weather; arrive early morning for shorter queues.
visitorInfo.howToReach: Inside the East Fort area of Thiruvananthapuram; the railway station and bus stand are a short drive away.
etiquette: Traditional dress is required: mundu/dhoti for men, saree or long skirt and blouse for women.
Entry to the inner temple is restricted to Hindus.
Leather items, mobile phones and cameras are not permitted inside; use the cloakroom.
Follow temple staff instructions and keep silence in the sanctum.
